title: Packing maximal induced matchings

problem.name_latex: Packing and partitioning maximal induced matchings
problem.name: Packing and partitioning maximal induced matchings
problem.statement_latex:
Let $\mathcal F$ contain all vertex sets $S\subseteq V$ such that every vertex of $G[S]$ has degree one and $S$ is inclusion-maximal with that property. Given $k$, find $k$ disjoint members of $\mathcal F$, or a partition of $V$ into $k$ such members. Each member is the endpoint set of an induced matching.
The quantum comparison uses QRAM time and classical subset-transform time, with bit complexity for the fixed-part-count Boolean encoding.
problem.statement_text: Let $\mathcal F$ contain all vertex sets $S\subseteq V$ such that every vertex of $G[S]$ has degree one and $S$ is inclusion-maximal with that property. Given $k$, find $k$ disjoint members of $\mathcal F$, or a partition of $V$ into $k$ such members. Each member is the endpoint set of an induced matching. The quantum comparison uses QRAM time and classical subset-transform time, with bit complexity for the fixed-part-count Boolean encoding.

quantum.details_latex: Restricted maximal-induced-matching enumeration has base $10^{1/5}$. Combining it with partial subset preprocessing and quantum search gives the bound for packing or exact partition into an unrestricted number of members. Membership includes both induced matching and maximality.
quantum.details_text: Restricted maximal-induced-matching enumeration has base $10^{1/5}$. Combining it with partial subset preprocessing and quantum search gives the bound for packing or exact partition into an unrestricted number of members. Membership includes both induced matching and maximality.

classical.details_latex: For every fixed number $q$ of members, a stronger bound is $O_{q,\epsilon}(2^{\epsilon n}\operatorname{poly}(n))$ for each fixed $\epsilon>0$. Vertex-membership and neighborhood-dominance bits encode degree one inside each member and exclusion of any further compatible edge. This uses $O(qn)$ variables and $O(qn)$ long clauses, together with polynomially many fixed-width clauses. Long-clause shortening followed by tensor contraction gives the bound; disjointness and complete coverage specify packing and partition respectively.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for unrestricted part count, arising from amplitude amplification. A fixed part count has the stronger subexponential classical comparator.
strength.description_text: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for unrestricted part count, arising from amplitude amplification. A fixed part count has the stronger subexponential classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum upper bound follows the framework theorem and the maximal-induced-matching enumeration bound. The classical fixed-$q$ conclusion follows the explicit Boolean encoding.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active registers represent selected endpoints, local degree and maximality conditions, with exponential coherent preprocessing memory. Large useful instances require fault tolerance and long coherent searches.
